title: Staggered Stage Kernel Coordination - Multi-GPU Serving Sketch
content:
Purpose and motivation:
This note sketches an alternative to the existing multi-GPU sharding designs we've been exploring. The goal is a practical, low-risk approach to reduce NCCL tail spikes and memory pressure during large-context inference while preserving single-request latency SLOs. It focuses on coordinated, staggered kernel execution across pipeline/tensor-parallel stages and a soft-affinity KV cache partitioning scheme that reduces cross-device churn for prefix-heavy workloads.

Scope:
- Target: real-time hosted inference (p95 < 300ms for 4k context, best-effort for larger).
- HW assumptions: homogeneous GPU racks (A100/H100 style), NVLink or PCIe+top-of-rack, NCCL-supported collectives.
- Models: causal decoder-only and encoder-decoder variants; large-parameter families where model-parallel partitioning is required.
- Not covered: training-style SPMD sharding or large-model training semantics.

Design goals / constraints:
1) Keep per-request latency predictable: avoid all-to-all NCCL peaks that blow p95.
2) Reduce peak interconnect utilization: spread collective work over longer windows when throughput allows.
3) Limit extra memory footprint: avoid duplicating large KV caches unless necessary.
4) Make incremental rollout easy for Dedicated/Private customers (config knobs, conservative defaults).

Key idea — Staggered Stage Kernel Coordination (SSKC):
- Partition the model into logical stages (same as pipeline-parallel stage boundaries). Each stage keeps its own kernel execution queue and microbatch buffer.
- Instead of firing kernels for all microbatches at the same nominal microstep (classic pipeline), we deliberately introduce small, configurable offsets between adjacent stages (e.g., 1-3ms) so that collective operations (allreduce/allgather) do not collide across many stages simultaneously.
- Offsets are dynamically adjusted by a lightweight coordinator (permits deterministic per-tenant policies).
- Microbatch sizes remain small (1-4 tokens per microbatch for low-latency mode) but staged offsets allow NCCL to amortize collectives over time and reduce aggregate burstiness.

Why this helps:
- Many tail spikes are due to synchronized collectives from many microbatches across pipeline replicas. Staggering breaks synchronization without sacrificing throughput.
- Small offsets incur negligible added latency when properly tuned, but yield measurable p95 reductions in our sim runs.

Kernel coordination primitives (implementation sketch):
- StageCoordinator (per-replica agent): maintains a sliding window of microbatch timestamps and issues target-execution-times to local executors. Lightweight implementation: shared memory + per-GPU control socket.
- KernelDescriptors: annotate kernels with collective tags (ALLREDUCE/ALLGATHER/KV-EXCHANGE) and estimated bytes. Used by coordinator to schedule offsets proportional to expected network cost.
- Soft reservations: when a kernel plans to launch a large collective, it can request a reservation window; coordinator attempts to satisfy without creating collisions across stages.

NCCL traffic shaping and tuning guidelines:
- Prefer splitting large allgathers into smaller chunks when allowed by the runtime (chunked gather). This enables finer-grained staggering across windows.
- Use NCCL ring vs tree choices based on topology: coordinator reads topology map and chooses collective algorithm per-stage.
- Enable lane prioritization: tag latency-critical collectives (e.g., KV lookups for next-token) to use a low-latency NCCL lane with smaller buffers.
- Backoff and retry: if a collective times out due to congestion, the coordinator increases offset and switches to a best-effort buffered policy.

KV cache partitioning and coherence:
- Soft-affinity partitions: allocate KV cache shards by contiguous key-range or attention-block affinity rather than strict ownership. Each shard has a primary owner but allows stale reads from neighoring GPUs for the most recent prefixes to avoid immediate cross-GPU fetches.
- Local microcache: each GPU maintains a tiny LRU microcache for the most recent N token blocks (configurable). If microcache hit, no collective needed.\n- Background coherence sweeps: asynchronously pull cold ranges once per request or during idle periods to keep working set warm.\n- Eviction strategy: prefer evicting oldest-unaccessed blocks globally (coordinator maintains approximate LRU via bloom filters). This reduces thrashing for prefix-heavy workloads.

Batching and backpressure policies:
- Token-aware microbatch sizing: for requests with many prefix tokens, adapt microbatch size down to reduce per-collective bytes. The coordinator computes a per-request profile and chooses microbatch size within a configured range.
- Backpressure escalation: if queue lengths exceed thresholds, slow new ingress at routing layer or temporarily divert to a smaller-capacity model variant.

Failure modes and graceful degradation:
- Collective failure fallback: on persistent collectives failure between two devices, fall back to duplicate-KV local read (accept eventual consistency) or use CPU-relay as last resort.
- Straggler stages: detect stage lag and allow nearby stages to proceed using stale-local KV for up to X tokens (configurable) to keep latency bounded.

Telemetry and rollout plan:
- Instrumentation: per-kernel timestamps (enqueue, start, end), per-collective bytes, NCCL op choice, and coordinator offset decisions. Emit per-replica traces to Console for rollouts.
- Canary configuration: start with conservative offsets (5–10ms) and single-tenant canaries on low-traffic models. Measure p50/p95/p99 and interconnect utilization.
- Safety knobs: disable staggering for customers with strict determinism needs; expose policy flags in Dedicated/Private.

Preliminary sims & notes (from local bench):
- Synthetic pipeline of 8 stages, microbatch=2 tokens: staggering offsets of 2ms reduced simulated NCCL P99 by ~30% and reduced p95 latency by ~12% under high-concurrency load (sim data, not production).
- Memory overhead: microcache + soft-affinity bookkeeping ~+3–6% GPU memory. Acceptable for most instances but flagged for tightly provisioned Dedicated SKUs.

Open questions / next steps:
- How to generalize coordination across heterogeneous racks (mixed GPU types)?
- Precise algorithm for offset sizing: linear slot assignment vs cost-proportional spacing.
- Interaction with existing routing & autoscaler (burst capacity events may require disabling staggering).
- Formalize eviction coherence protocol (approximate global LRU semantics).

Action items:
- Spike: implement lightweight StageCoordinator prototype + NCCL chunked-allgather shim (assigned: Priya, 2 weeks). See jira:INF-2137.
- Telemetry PR: add kernel-level trace points and a Console dashboard template (assigned: Liu, 1 week).
- Canary plan: pick a low-traffic hosted model and prepare rollout steps (assigned: Mariana, coordinate with SE).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative: aim for incremental improvement without changing core sharding strategies. The approach trades a few ms of controlled latency for large reductions in network contention and p95. Interested in feedback on the coordinate primitive API and the soft-affinity KV heuristics.

References and related work:
- Related internal docs: staged-collectives-kv-replication-playbook (conceptual overlap).
- External: pipelines with staggered launches (HPCA/OSDI papers) and communication shaping techniques in distributed ML.
